Separate regional fund, per the firm's 2012 rebrand coverage. TechCrunch (15 Jul 2012) says BV's people ran five regional funds (US, Europe, Asia, Russia, South America), 'each under a different name', and after the rebrand kept 'dedicated funds in five regions', the Eastern Europe one to be called 'e.ventures Russia', each with 'a dedicated local investment team'. It does not give the pre-2012 name of the Russian vehicle, and no fund name, manager entity or filing for a standalone e.ventures Russia fund was found. Two signals point the other way for later deals: (1) tech.eu (2015) names the CarPrice seed investor 'eVenture Capital Partners', the Hamburg-based ex-Otto Group vehicle behind e.ventures Europe (the firm's own 2012 news feed calls it 'Ottos eVC Partners'), so the Oct 2014 CarPrice seed may have been booked through the European entity; (2) part of the Russian book was held through Fastlane Ventures, the Moscow company builder co-founded by Oskar Hartmann: Fastlane.png sits on the 2016 wall, the firm's news feed carried Fastlane's 2012-2013 raises (VTB Capital, Kenges Rakishev), and Fastlane-backed Domgeo and Pinme sat on the 2012 wall. The Japanese desk also invested into Russia (feed post 'japanese-venture-fund-invests-in-teamo-ru', 2012). People named on the site: Alexandra Rasskazova, Elena Fironova (headshots uploaded 2012-2016). Rows here tagged Russia: carprice, domgeo, pinme, onlinetours.
